questions.q: You want to greet your best friend. Which question fits?
questions.explanation: A friend your own age is a tú relationship, so the tú-form estás is correct.

questions.q: You're greeting your school principal for the first time. Which question fits?
questions.explanation: An adult in a position of authority you've just met calls for the formal usted.

questions.q: In Latin American Spanish, which word means 'you all' for any group — close friends or strangers alike?
questions.explanation: Latin American Spanish uses ustedes for every group; vosotros is used in Spain, not this course's dialect.

questions.q: Which pair of words names the two levels of politeness Spanish speakers choose between when addressing someone?
questions.explanation: Formal and informal are the two registers; tú/usted are the pronouns that express them.
Saludar means 'to greet' — despedirse is its opposite, 'to say goodbye.'
Despedirse means 'to say goodbye,' completing the conversation that saludar starts.
